newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Kohl modifies support for Romania in NATO.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl modifies support for Romania in NATO.

text.p: A Bonn government spokesman said on Thursday recent remarks by Chancellor Helmut Kohl in favour of Romania joining NATO in a first wave of new members should not be seen as a definitive vote of support.
Kohl's backing for Romania at a summit of mainly Christian Democrat groups in Strasbourg earlier this week had been an initial "expression of sympathy", the spokesman said in response to enquiries.
NATO is due to announce at a summit in Madrid in July which eastern European countries will be invited to begin negotiations for membership in 1999.
The U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday voted in favour of NATO expansion and designated Romania as one of the nations eligible for U.S. assistance in seeking membership.
But the U.S. Senate, concerned about the costs, is particularly reluctant to see a large group of new members joining the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation in the near future.
Other leading candidates include Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
Romania in particular has staged a high-profile campaign for NATO membership ahead of the Madrid summit and the issue has become a major topic of domestic debate.
